elements.label: Idle before cycle
elements.observed: Three loose parts on the table: blue 2×2 slope, pink 1×6 brick, white 4×6 plate. No hands.

elements.label: Reach and grasp pink 1×6 brick
elements.observed: One hand enters from the top right, closes on the pink brick and lifts it.

elements.flag: Overlaps the pick: both hands working at once.
elements.label: Hold the base plate
elements.observed: Second hand enters from the bottom and grips the near edge of the plate.

elements.label: Place pink brick on plate
elements.observed: Pink brick lowered lengthwise onto the plate, second stud column in camera view.

elements.flag: Longest element. Pressing force and click are not visible.
elements.label: Press pink brick down
elements.observed: Fingers stay on the brick and press along it; the hand hides most of the brick.

elements.flag: Half-built piece turned mid-cycle; reason not visible.
elements.label: Reach and grasp blue 2×2 slope
elements.observed: Hand releases the pink brick, moves to the blue slope and picks it up. The other hand turns the half-built piece about 30–45°.

elements.label: Carry blue slope
elements.observed: Blue slope moved to the half-built piece.

elements.flag: Possible in-hand turn; a re-grip or re-placement can't be confirmed.
elements.label: Position and orient blue slope
elements.observed: Slope held at an angle against the side of the pink brick; appears to turn in the fingers before going down.

elements.label: Press blue slope down
elements.observed: Both hands on the assembly, mostly hidden. By about 4.8 s the slope is visible lying flat to the right of the pink brick.

elements.label: Release and set down
elements.observed: Assembly turned back to its starting angle and put down; both hands out of frame by 5.6 s.

elements.flag: No hands in view, so the shift is inferred to be camera movement.
elements.label: Idle after cycle
elements.observed: Finished assembly alone on the table. Its position and size in frame shift, mostly after about 7.0 s.

finalState.note: Pink 1×6 brick on the plate's second stud column, full length. Blue 2×2 slope over columns 3–4, rows 3–4, studs next to the pink brick, slope facing outward. One white column left free. Matches the attached reference photos viewed from the opposite end.

label: Baseline
limitations: Seating can't be confirmed: both pressing elements are hidden by hands, so presses can't be counted and a lift-and-replace can't be ruled out. Snap sounds in the audio track were not analyzed.
One cycle only: no way yet to say whether 5.5 s is typical or whether turning the piece is method or a one-off.
No written standard work, so only the final state was compared, against the reference photos.
Top-down 2D view: no height or gap information; parts were identified by counting studs.
Blank background: camera movement can't be fully separated from object movement.
Not visible: defects such as cracks or shade differences, operator intent, and anything before recording started.
processData: Cycle start and end (hands enter and leave the work area) and cycle time
Element sequence, checkable against a standard order
Time per element, e.g. pressing took about 2.4 s of the 5.5 s cycle (about 44%)
Parts handled: 3 of 3, each once, no drops or repeated picks
Two-hand overlap: second hand busy from 0.6 s to 5.6 s
Handling events: 1 re-orientation of the half-built piece, 1 possible re-grip, 0 confirmed repeats
Final-state check against a reference image: parts present, placement, slope direction
Confidence per element: how much of it was hidden by hands

source.note: Claude Code, frame by frame at 0.1 s steps, reviewed in chat

statusNote: Each of the three parts was handled once in a clear order and nothing was dropped. The finished layout matches the reference photos. One cycle only, so there is no baseline variance yet; flags are observations, not deviations.
